newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - SE Asian prices steady despite weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - SE Asian prices steady despite weak demand.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are expected to trend steadily this week despite soft demand as supplies remain tight after the Chinese Lunar New Year and Hari Raya holiday period, regional traders said on Monday.
The onset of the wintering period in the main natural rubber-producing countries of Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia should also provide some support for prices, they said.
But traders said weak demand from major consumers in Europe, the U.S. and Japan will curtail the upside potential for prices.
"I don't think people are going to rush in to buy," a rubber trader in Kuala Lumpur told Reuters. "If there is going to be any (price) build-up, it'll be gradual."

"We're in the wintering period, but it doesn't seem to be helping prices because there's no buying coming in," a dealer for a North American trading house based in Singapore added. "The result of this is that prices will just consolidate."
Traders in the city-state said ample stocks in China and Europe will also keep buying to a minimum.
In Indonesia, dealers said there had been some sporadic buying from European and U.S. buyers, but orders were tiny and only reached between 100 and 200 tonnes.
The benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 March rubber price was quoted at 54.50 U.S. cents a lb FOB Medan, Surabaya and Palembang.
In Padang, offer prices were unchanged at 54.25 cents, while in Pontianak and Jambi traders offered SIR20 at 53.75 cents.
Traders said buyers seemed to be waiting for prices to ease slightly and sellers may have to give up trying to hold the 54.00 U.S. cents a lb offer level.
"The problem is that traders have been too stubborn in that they keep increasing the offer prices, while in fact there are not so many buyers coming to the market," said one trader.
"There is always a trend in the market that once the price falls, it will continue that way," said another trader.
Supplies remain tight because farmers have yet to return to work after the Eid al-Fitr celebration earlier this month.
More buyers should enter the market next week as they need to replenish their stocks for March, April and May.
In Malaysia, some activity is expected in the market this week although prices are expected to stay at current levels, or even soften, as demand is still weak.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted benchmark RSS1 at 304 Malaysian cents a kg at the close of the market on Friday, and the SMR20 was indicated at 299.50, both for March buyer.
Traders reported ample supplies of latex and other raw materials in the market. Drum latex was offered by trading houses at 236-238 cents a kg FOB on Friday.

They said most institutional buyers from Europe and the United States have met their quota for rubber until the first quarter of 1997, but added the market may see some short-covering in the meantime.
Thai rubber prices were firm last week in slow trade as sellers withheld stocks in anticipation of further rises, industry sources said.

"Prices continued an upward trend in line with the rise in the Japan market," said a Hat Yai-based trader. "But market activities were very slow. People did not want to sell rubber as they expected prices will rise further."
The benchmark RSS3 for March shipment was quoted at around US$1.23 kg FOB Bangkok on Friday from $1.19 a kg on the same basis the previous week, traders said.
Latex was quoted at around $0.94 a kg for March delivery against $0.92 a kg the previous week, traders said.
(With contributions from Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
